papers.title: Phenological divergence between flowering plants and flower-visiting Lepidoptera under climate change across Europe.
papers.abstract: Climate change is altering life-cycle timing and may disrupt coordinated interactions between flowering plants and flower-visiting insects. Using Global Biodiversity Information Facility observation records from Europe between 2000 and 2024, we compiled a continental-scale phenological dataset covering flowering periods of 707 angiosperm species and adult activity periods of 620 Lepidoptera species. We extracted the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles and activity-window width and used linear mixed-effects models to analyse spatio-temporal trends. The results showed that plant phenology advanced significantly, with the 10th and 50th percentiles shifting earlier by -0.597 and -0.507 d yr⁻¹, respectively, whereas the 90th percentile showed no significant change; flowering-window width increased by 0.361 d yr⁻¹. By contrast, Lepidoptera phenology advanced evenly across the season, with the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles shifting by -0.137, -0.153 and -0.155 d yr⁻¹, respectively, while activity-window width showed no significant change. Because flowering plants advanced faster than Lepidoptera in the early and middle season, plant-insect phenological overlap declined at 0.340 d yr⁻¹, indicating increasing mismatch across Europe. Further analyses identified temperature as the dominant driver of phenological advance in both groups, but flowering plants and Lepidoptera differed in their responses to other climatic factors. These results suggest that climate change is weakening phenological synchrony between flowering plants and flower-visiting Lepidoptera, with potential consequences for pollination and ecosystem functioning.

papers.title: Regulation of hepatic stellates cell activation by biomimetic fibrotic hydrogels with uniform and heterogeneous matrix stiffness.
papers.abstract: Current research on liver fibrosis predominantly relies on culture matrices with uniform stiffness, largely overlooking the pathophysiological relevance of stiffness heterogeneity-the spatially uneven stiffness distribution characteristic of fibrotic liver tissue. To address this, we engineered biomimetic fibrotic hydrogels using decellularized liver matrix (DLM) from fibrotic tissues and methacrylated hyaluronic acid (MeHA). These hydrogels replicated the distinct stiffness profiles of normal, earlystage fibrotic, and late-stage fibrotic liver. Using a custom honeycomb-shaped mold, we integrated them into a unified platform featuring both uniform and heterogeneous mechanical regions. By co-culturing hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) on this platform, we investigated how matrix stiffness regulates HSCs proliferation, migration, and activation. Results demonstrated that on uniformly stiff substrates, particularly those mimicking late-stage fibrosis, ECM components and high stiffness promoted HSCs activation, upregulated the Piezo1-YAP signaling axis. In contrast, although the lowstiffness region of the mechanically heterogeneous platform exhibited increased HSC proliferation and activation, the proliferation and activation levels in the medium-and high-stiffness regions were significantly reduced. The expression patterns of the Piezo1-YAP signaling pathway further corroborated this phenomenon. These findings suggest that mechanical heterogeneity may exert a negative regulatory effect on HSC activation. This study provides new insights into the mechanobiological mechanisms underlying hepatic fibrosis and reveals potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: HSPiP, computational, and thermodynamic models-based solubility validation of tofacitinib in PEG400 - water system, shelf-life estimation, and GastroPlus-enabled predictive in vivo performance.
papers.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The subcutaneous (sub-Q) delivery of tofacitinib citrate (TOFA) can be a promising alternative to overcome oral associated side effects and complications . OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to address HSPiP based predicted solubility and solubility behaviour of TOFA in various mass ratios (m = 0.0-1.0) of PEG400 in PEG400-water system T = 298.15-318.15 K. METHODS: Hansen solubility parameters were estimated and the experimental solubility data were validated using various models (Van't Hoff, Apelblat, Roseman-Yalkowsky, and thermodynamic models). Finally, the stability study was conducted to estimate TOFA shelf-life, followed by GastroPlus-based predictive in vivo performance in humans. RESULTS: PEG400 addition resulted in reduced δand δvalues up to m = 0.5, which may be correlated to the effective disruption of extensive H-bond network strength and decreased overall polarity of water by PEG400, as predicted in HSPiP. The temperature-dependent solubility was validated with the models. The binary system (m = 0.5) exhibited stable solubility, suitable for sub-Q delivery. The enthalpy-entropy compensation temperature (T) was 59.5 °C, suggesting constant ΔG° over m = 0.1-0.9 of PEG400. Thus, TOFA solubility and stability were temperature, mass, and pH dependent. GastroPlus software predicted improved pharmacokinetic parameters and extended in vivo absorption following sub-Q delivery at m = 0.5 in humans. CONCLUSION: Thus, a stable sub-Q product can be a promising alternative to the conventional tablet of TOFA.

papers.title: Sensory processing sensitivity profiles and self-reported mental effort and concentration across pedagogical contexts among social services and healthcare students: a cross-sectional study.
papers.journal: Advances in health sciences education : theory and practice
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Changes in higher education and evolving pedagogical practices have increased the diversity of cognitive, emotional, and social demands experienced by students, highlighting the need to understand individual differences, including sensory processing sensitivity (SPS). AIM: To identify SPS profiles among social services and healthcare students and examine whether self-reported mental effort and concentration across selected pedagogical contexts differed between the profiles. DESIGN: A cross-sectional study. PARTICIPANTS: 1185 social and healthcare higher education students across Finland. METHODS: The data were collected with the SPS Questionnaire (43 items) during 2024-2025. K-means clustering and One-way ANOVA were employed to analyse the profiles of SPS. The associated pedagogical factors were analysed using Chi-square tests. The STROBE guidelines were followed. RESULTS: Five distinct SPS profiles emerged, differing significantly in sensitivity, emotional reactivity, and pedagogical responses. Profiles characterised by higher emotional and physiological reactivity (Profiles 2, 4, and 5) generally reported greater mental effort and more concentration difficulties, particularly in socially demanding and performance-based situations such as group work, oral presentations, and simulations. In contrast, low-reactive profiles (Profiles 1 and 3) demonstrated stable concentration and lower cognitive load across learning contexts. CONCLUSIONS: Pedagogical methods do not influence all students equally. Instructional approaches that involve intense social interaction, performance exposure, or high cognitive demands may disproportionately increase stress and cognitive load for highly reactive learners. Designing inclusive, psychologically safe, and adaptive learning environments that consider SPS-related differences can support student well-being, learning effectiveness, and sustainable professional development in social and healthcare education.

papers.title: Bcl11a preserves hematopoietic stem cell function in culture by restraining Ncf1-dependent ROS.
papers.abstract: Ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) is limited by culture-induced oxidative stress, yet the upstream transcriptional drivers remain poorly defined. Here, we show that the transcription factor Bcl11a is rapidly and persistently downregulated during HSC culture and that this decline drives functional deterioration. Bcl11a was both required and sufficient to maintain quiescence, clonogenic activity, and serially transplantable HSC function. Mechanistically, Bcl11a directly represses a Nox2 NADPH oxidase gene module, including Ncf1, encoding the p47phox organizer subunit; Ncf1 deletion reduced ROS and partially rescued the defects of Bcl11a-deficient HSCs. Rapamycin-but not the ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine-restored Bcl11a expression, suppressed Ncf1 and ROS, and improved HSC function, identifying Bcl11a as a candidate effector linking mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibition to redox control. This axis was conserved in human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, revealing a druggable transcriptional vulnerability of cultured HSCs and a framework for improving ex vivo-expanded grafts.

papers.title: Hinokitiol alleviates liver fibrosis in rats: Plausible role of hepatic stellate cell activation and TGF-β/Smad2/3 axis.
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis represents a progressive pathological condition with excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, primarily driven by hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) activation and sustained inflammatory and oxidative stress responses. Despite its clinical burden, effective antifibrotic therapies remain limited. Here, we investigated the therapeutic potential of hinokitiol (HKT), a natural tropolone derivative, in attenuating liver fibrosis using both in vitro and in vivo models. Human LX-2 HSCs were employed to assess the mechanistic effects of HKT under TGF-β-induced fibrogenic conditions. HKT treatment significantly suppressed myofibroblastic transdifferentiation, as evidenced by downregulation of α-SMA, N-cadherin, vimentin, and collagen I, and reduced HSC migration. Additionally, HKT attenuated reactive oxygen species generation via inhibition of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4) expression. In an experimental model of alcohol- and carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced liver fibrosis, oral administration of HKT (2.5, 5, and 10 mg/kg) significantly ameliorated hepatic injury, as indicated by reduced serum ALT and AST levels, improved liver morphology, and restored hepatic architecture. Histopathological and biochemical analyses revealed a pronounced reduction in collagen deposition, hydroxyproline content, and fibrotic bridging. Mechanistically, HKT suppressed the TGF-β/Smad2/3 cascade, thereby inhibiting HSCs activation and ECM accumulation. Furthermore, HKT reduced the expression of lysyl oxidase-like 2 (LOXL2) protein, which further impeded the stiffening of fibrous liver. In addition, HKT mitigated hepatic oxidative stress, while concurrently attenuating pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-1β. Taken together, our findings establish HKT as a potential candidate to limit fibrosis progression and hepatic tissue remodeling by impeding HSCs activation and the TGF-β/Smad2/3/LOXL2 cascade.

papers.title: TDQ-Cl ameliorates hepatic fibrosis-associated inflammation and intestinal injury through regulating RXRα-STAT3 signaling.
papers.abstract: Hepatic fibrosis is sustained by inflammation-driven hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) activation and is frequently accompanied by intestinal barrier disruption and gut microbial dysbiosis. 2,3,9,10-tetramethoxy-5,6-dihydroisoquinolino[3,2-a]isoquinolin-7-ium chloride (TDQ-Cl) is a quaternary isoquinoline alkaloid with anti-inflammatory activity and emerging hepatoprotective potential. This study investigated the hepatoprotective effects and underlying mechanisms of TDQ-Cl against hepatic fibrosis and associated intestinal injury. HSC-T6 and LX-2 were activated by transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) and treated with TDQ-Cl, retinoic acid (RA), LG100268 or UVI 3003. RXRα-silenced LX-2 was stimulated with TGF-β and treated with TDQ-Cl. C57BL/6 J mice were intraperitoneally injected with thioacetamide (TAA), followed by TDQ-Cl, silymarin or RA administration. In activated HSCs, TDQ-Cl reduced extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation, IL-6, cleaved caspase-1, mature IL-1β, and STAT3 phosphorylation while restoring RXRα expression. Cellular thermal shift assay showed increased thermal stability of RXRα following TDQ-Cl treatment. RXRα silencing exacerbated fibrotic responses and attenuated the inhibitory effects of TDQ-Cl on p-STAT3, α-SMA, and IL-6. Co-immunoprecipitation indicated that TDQ-Cl reduced the association between RXRα and phosphorylated STAT3. TDQ-Cl also attenuated conditioned-medium-induced LX-2 activation, accompanied by regulation of RXRα-STAT3 signaling. In TAA-induced mice, TDQ-Cl attenuated liver injury, ECM accumulation, inflammation, and hepatic STAT3 phosphorylation while restoring hepatic RXRα expression. TDQ-Cl also improved intestinal barrier integrity, reduced macrophage infiltration and STAT3 phosphorylation, restored colonic RXRα expression, and partially normalized TAA-associated gut microbial alterations. papers.title: Aqueous Ammonium Ion Hybrid Supercapacitor: A Diffusion Dynamics Perspective.
papers.abstract: Aqueous ammonium-ion hybrid supercapacitors (A-HSCs) have emerged as a promising energy storage technology, offering intrinsic safety, low cost, environmental sustainability. However, the realization of these advantages hinges critically on the diffusion dynamics of the ammonium ion (NH), which remain incompletely understood and require systematic elucidation of the underlying mechanisms and optimization strategies. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in NHdiffusion kinetics within A-HSCs, approached from three interconnected perspectives: electrode materials, electrolyte engineering, and charge carrier structure. We systematically summarize the kinetic characteristics and structural design strategies for four representative classes of electrode materials-layered compounds, tunnel structures, Prussian blue analogs (PBAs), and organic frameworks-that govern NHtransport. In parallel, we elucidate how concentrated electrolytes, additive electrolytes, and high-entropy electrolytes (HEEs) reconfigure the hydrogen-bond network of water to modulate the solvation environment. Furthermore, we explore the unique diffusion behavior arising from the intrinsic tetrahedral geometry of NHand the influence of hydrogen isotope substitution, which provides a powerful experimental lever for disentangling the coupled contributions of mass, rotational inertia, and hydrogen-bond strength to the diffusion dynamics. Finally, we identify current limitations and challenges, and outline future directions for the development of high-performance aqueous ammonium-ion energy storage devices.

papers.title: Hepatic Stellate Cells: Fibrogenic Effectors to Central Regulators of Metabolism, Liver Disease Signaling, and Systemic Crosstalk.
papers.abstract: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) have long been regarded as the core effector cells in liver fibrosis. The advent of single-cell omics and metabolomics has led to a paradigm shift in our understanding of these cells. Notably, they are not only implicated in local fibrosis but are being increasingly recognized as a hub integrating metabolic and immune signaling. Located at the interface between hepatic vasculature and parenchyma, HSCs have the capacity to modulate intestinal barrier function, neurotransmitter circulation, myocardial energy metabolism, and bone remodeling through metabolic reprogramming (enhanced glycolysis, vitamin A consumption, glutamine metabolism remodeling) and receptor signaling (TLR4, TGF-β, CXCR4, etc.), as well as by secreting metabolites, exosomal miRNAs, and cytokines. Concurrently, HSCs perceive feedback signals from these organs, forming a dynamic cross-organ feedback network. This review systematically integrates the metabolic characteristics of HSCs in diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, chronic viral hepatitis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, along with their cross-organ interactive effects. We further discuss intervention strategies targeting metabolic pathways, exosomal cargo, and the microbiota-metabolism axis, and propose a three-tier translational framework stratifying HSC-targeted therapeutic approaches by developmental stage, offering novel insights for shifting liver disease treatment from single antifibrotic approaches toward systemic, multi-organ precision interventions.

papers.title: Ginsenoside Rh1 exerts hepatoprotective effects against liver fibrosis through induction of ferroptosis via SLC7A11 inhibition.
papers.journal: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a critical pathological stage in the progression from chronic liver disease to cirrhosis, and the exploration of preventive agents derived from traditional Chinese medicine offers considerable potential. However, the precise role and molecular mechanism of ginsenoside Rh1 (Rh1) in liver fibrosis remain largely obscure. This study investigated the anti-fibrotic mechanism of Rh1, focusing on ferroptosis. In vitro, Rh1 dose-dependently suppressed the viability of activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and concurrently induced key ferroptosis features. In vivo, Rh1 administration markedly attenuated carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis, improved histological architecture, and restored liver function. Mechanistically, transcriptomic analysis and molecular validation identified SLC7A11, a core regulator of ferroptosis, as a binding partner of Rh1. Rescue experiments confirmed that the pro-ferroptotic and anti-fibrotic effects of Rh1 were functionally dependent on SLC7A11 inhibition. In conclusion, our findings demonstrated that ginsenoside Rh1 alleviated liver fibrosis by targeting SLC7A11 to promote the ferroptosis in cultured HSCs, unveiling a novel pharmacological mechanism. This work provided a compelling preclinical rationale for developing Rh1 as a promising preventive agent against liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Heat-induced translational suppression is associated with initiator tRNA degradation in thermotolerant cells.
papers.abstract: Heat stress induces multiple stress responses, including translational suppression, upregulation of heat shock proteins (HSPs), and RNA degradation. Transient exposure to heat stress also induces thermotolerance. Thermotolerant cells exhibit transient resistance to subsequent stress and reduced translational suppression and apoptotic cell death. Thermotolerance is closely correlated with the upregulation of HSPs. Heat stress induces translational suppression via degradation of the initiator tRNA (iMet). In this study, we investigated the relationship between iMet expression and translational suppression in re-exposed cells and examined how these processes are associated with cell death following re-exposure to heat stress. Translational suppression was closely correlated with iMet expression in re-exposed cells, and the pattern of apoptosis was similar to that of translational activity and iMet expression. The expression patterns of HSP27 and HSP70 showed a weak association with apoptosis. The temporal patterns of translational activity, iMet expression, and apoptosis after the initial heat stress suggest a possible association among these thermotolerant responses.

papers.title: Pot1a maintains mesenchymal stem cell niche function to support hematopoietic stem cells.
papers.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) maintain their function through interactions with niche cells in the bone marrow. We previously demonstrated that protection of telomeres 1a (Pot1a), a shelterin component, maintains HSCs and neuron-glial antigen 2-expressing (NG2) mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) by suppressing DNA damage response (DDR) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. However, the role of Pot1a in leptin receptor-expressing (LepR) MSCs, a primary HSC niche component, remains unclear. LepR-specific Pot1a knockout mice showed decreased LepRMSC numbers, increased DDR and ROS production, reduced HSC quiescence, and impaired long-term hematopoietic reconstitution. In contrast, cell-permeable Pot1a enhanced the hematopoietic-supporting function of LepRMSCs. Pot1a deficiency reduced pleiotrophin (Ptn) expression, whereas Pot1a overexpression increased its expression. These findings suggest that Pot1a preserves LepRMSC function by limiting stress-associated changes, maintaining MSC numbers, and regulating hematopoietic-supportive factor expression, including PTN.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Triggered HSC Membrane-Cloaked Nanotherapeutics Attenuate Liver Fibrosis via Simultaneous Modulation of Mitophagic Flux and the TGF-β/Smad3 Cascade.
papers.abstract: This study presents an ultrasound-triggered therapeutic platform based on melatonin-loaded and perfluoropentane-encapsulated mesoporous silica nanoparticles, which are further cloaked with activated hepatic stellate cell membranes (HM-Mel@PFP-MSNs), designed for the precision treatment of liver fibrosis. This innovative drug delivery system leverages the inherent targeting properties of cell membrane coatings, effectively functioning as a "gatekeeper" that prevents premature drug release. By incorporating melatonin and perfluoropentane (PFP), our approach enables ultrasound-mediated controlled release, enhancing therapeutic efficacy. In vitro investigations revealed that upon ultrasound activation, HM-Mel@PFP-MSNs significantly inhibited the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and alleviated mitochondrial damage. Mechanistic studies employing Western blot analysis revealed that this nanotherapeutic strategy was associated with altered expression of autophagy-related proteins, including a reduced LC3-II/I ratio, increased P62 accumulation, and downregulated PINK1/Parkin. These findings suggest an overall suppression of autophagic activity, encompassing both general autophagy and mitophagy; however, a causal link remains to be established. Furthermore, using a rat model of liver fibrosis, robust histological assessments (including HE, Masson, Sirius Red, and α-SMA staining) demonstrated that our system markedly ameliorated fibrotic lesions under precise ultrasound guidance. This research introduces a novel strategy that integrates targeted delivery, controlled drug release, and visualizable therapeutic outcomes, thereby representing a significant advancement in the management of liver diseases. By simultaneously modulating mitophagic flux and the TGF-β/Smad3 signaling cascade, our HM-Mel@PFP-MSN-based nanotherapeutics open new avenues for liver fibrosis treatment, emphasizing the potential of leveraging ultrasound in enhancing therapeutic precision

papers.title: CMTM6 regulates hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis through modulating IFNRs-STAT1-KLF4 signaling axis.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: CMTM6 is known to stabilize PD-L1 on cancer cells, facilitating immune evasion, but its role in normal hematopoiesis remains unexplored. Hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) homeostasis is tightly regulated by interferon (IFN) signaling, yet the mechanisms controlling IFN receptor stability are unclear. OBJECTIVES: In this study we investigated whether CMTM6 regulates HSC maintenance and elucidated the underlying molecular pathways. METHODS: Using a conditional Cmtm6 knockout mouse model (Vav-Cre), we performed flow cytometry, competitive transplantation, single-cell RNA sequencing, co-immunoprecipitation, and functional assays on bone marrow HSCs. RESULTS: Cmtm6 deficiency led to increased HSC proliferation but impaired reconstitution capacity, accompanied by elevated DNA damage and disrupted cell polarity. Single-cell analysis revealed a marked reduction in IFN response pathways. Mechanistically, CMTM6 directly interacted with IFNAR1 and IFNGR1, stabilizing their protein expression. Downstream, Cmtm6 deletion impaired STAT1 phosphorylation and reduced KLF4 expression; single-cell analysis revealed a significant positive correlation between Stat1 activity and Klf4 expression, and STAT1 inhibition in HSCs confirmed that STAT1 activity is required for maintaining KLF4 expression. Notably, KLF4 overexpression partially rescued colony-forming defects and reduced γH2AX foci in Cmtm6-deficient HSCs, identifying KLF4 as a key downstream effector. Additionally, we observed accompanying molecular changes including reduced SIAH2, elevated DYRK2, decreased c-MYC, and increased P53, which may contribute to the observed phenotypes. CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that CMTM6 maintains HSC homeostasis by stabilizing IFN receptors and regulating the IFNR-STAT1-KLF4 signaling axis, revealing a novel physiological function for CMTM6 in hematopoiesis.

papers.title: Imaging and Analyzing the Macrophages that Regulate Pathological Hematopoietic Clones in the Mouse Calvarial Bone Marrow.
papers.abstract: The bone marrow microenvironment has been shown to regulate the progression of myeloid neoplasms. Given that bone remodeling is a dynamic process that releases bone particles as danger molecules into the bone marrow space, different stages of bone turnover across marrow cavities can impose spatial heterogeneity of inflammatory responses that impact both healthy and mutant hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Specifically, macrophages, serving as critical members in the HSC niche, can adopt either pro-inflammatory (M1) or anti-inflammatory (M2) phenotypes based on these local signals, which results in distinct surface receptor expression and cytokine secretion. Using intravital microscopy, a murine model of Tet2 deficiency (a prevalent mutation across the spectrum of myeloid disorders), and labeling strategies to track marrow macrophages, our recent work identified compartmentalized inflammatory landscapes in the bone marrow that differentially support expansion of mutant cells. In this chapter, we describe detailed protocols to track pathological clones with respect to marrow macrophage in live mouse calvaria, and protocols of image-guided bone button isolation to analyze pro-inflammatory cytokines from the marrow cavities of interest. These protocols can also be integrated with cell isolation for single-cell transcriptomic profiling or downstream functional assessments. The labeling strategies may be applied to image macrophages in other tissue types.

papers.title: ASIC1a promotes liver fibrosis by inhibiting METTL3 SUMOylation.
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis represents a major global health burden, with its core pathological feature being the excessive deposition of extracellular matrix driven by activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). Acid-sensitive ion channel 1a (ASIC1a) has been shown to be associated with the progression of liver fibrosis, but the molecular mechanisms by which it regulates RNA mA methylation remain unclear. The aim of this study is to investigate the role of ASIC1a in liver fibrosis and the specific regulatory pathways involved. Experiments were conducted using human liver fibrosis tissue, a carbon tetrachloride-induced mouse model of liver fibrosis, and rat hepatic stellate cells; a mouse model with a hepatic stellate cell-specific ASIC1a knockout was generated; performed RIP-qPCR to validate METTL3 binding to target transcripts, while global mA levels were assessed by dot blot and methyltransferase activity assays, the molecular mechanisms were elucidated using methods such as immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, SUMOylation assays, and quantitative m⁶A methylation analysis. ASIC1a is significantly up-regulated in fibrotic liver tissue and activated hepatic stellate cells; specific knockout of ASIC1a significantly reduces the severity of liver fibrosis in mice. Mechanistically, ASIC1a binds to SAE1 to inhibit the SUMOylation of METTL3, thereby enhancing its mA methyltransferase activity, which in turn promotes the activation of hepatic stellate cells and the progression of fibrosis. This study has revealed a novel ASIC1a-METTL3-mA de-SUMOylation regulatory axis in the progression of liver fibrosis, suggesting that ASIC1a may serve as a potential target for anti-fibrotic therapy.

papers.title: Stochastic and quantum perspectives on teleost immunity: Linking immunogenetics, structure, and biophysics.
papers.journal: Progress in biophysics and molecular biology
papers.abstract: Teleost fishes possess highly diverse, lineage-specific pattern-recognition receptor (PRR) repertoires shaped by teleost-specific whole-genome duplication (3R-WGD), subsequent duplication, differential retention, functional divergence, and gene loss. Toll-like, RIG-I-like, and NOD-like receptor families show lineage-specific expansion and, in some cases, adaptive sequence evolution, particularly in regions implicated in ligand recognition. Separately, hydrogen tunneling is supported in specific enzyme reactions, while radical-pair chemistry provides a bounded mechanistic precedent rather than evidence for teleost immune function. This review examines whether teleost PRR diversification creates concrete, testable opportunities for investigating analogous biophysical mechanisms, without assuming that receptor diversity or environmental sensitivity entails non-classical effects. A five-level evidence hierarchy is applied: direct teleost evidence, evidence from other systems, indirect teleost evidence, testable hypothesis, and unsupported or contradicted claim. No direct evidence was identified for a functionally consequential quantum-biological mechanism in teleost immune recognition or signaling. However, increasing genomic, structural, transcriptomic, single-cell, and functional-genomic resolution provides a tractable framework for testing such possibilities. Sequence and structural divergence among PRR paralogs can be evaluated using structure prediction, molecular dynamics, and, where chemically justified, quantum-chemical or QM/MM methods, with uncertainty assessed across stages and experimental validation through ligand binding, signaling, and environmental-response phenotypes. The NADPH-to-flavin hydride-transfer step in an immune effector oxidase is proposed as a chemically defined candidate, not an established teleost tunneling mechanism. Quantum mechanisms therefore remain hypotheses rather than established features of teleost immunity. A falsifiable research

papers.title: The orthographic mind: Orthographic imagery propensity correlates with semantic structure and sensory sensitivity.
papers.abstract: Individuals differ in their habitual use of internal representational modes, including visual imagery, internal verbalization, and orthographic imagery (the mental simulation of written word forms). The present research examined whether such internal representational propensities relate to semantic organization and external information engagement. Across two studies (total N = 1,399), we assessed individuals' internal representational modes using the Internal Representations Questionnaire and examined their associations with semantic structure (nine-word semantic rating experiments; N = 1,109) and external information engagement (sensory-processing sensitivity and mobile app usage). Orthographic imagery showed robust associations with both semantic geometry and external information engagement patterns: Individuals with stronger orthographic imagery showed greater cross-category semantic association strength, lower semantic conformity, and lower sensory-processing sensitivity. Internal verbalization was positively associated with within-category semantic cohesion, while visual imagery showed no reliable associations with semantic geometry and limited associations with real-world media engagement. Effects were modest but consistent across experiments. These findings suggest that internal representational modes function as stable weighting biases, subtly modulating semantic geometry and sensory-processing profiles. Such propensities therefore correspond to structured variations in cognition, rather than merely phenomenological differences in inner experience. papers.title: CSE1L enrichment in pediatric and young adult acute myeloid leukemia reveals a ribosomal export dependency.
papers.abstract: Proteins shuttle between the nucleus and cytoplasm through the nuclear pore and via nuclear transport receptors, termed importins and exportins. Although genetic alterations involving nucleoporins are enriched in pediatric, adolescent, and young adult (AYA) acute myeloid leukemia (AML), nucleocytoplasmic transport has not been extensively studied in this disease. We discover that genes encoding nucleocytoplasmic transport pathway components (Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes [KEGG]: hsa03013) are enriched in AML cells from younger patients (≤40 years). Within this pathway, CSE1L is the highest expressed exportin in pediatric/AYA AML and shows minimal expression in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). CSE1L depletion reduces leukemic cell growth, proliferation, and clonogenic capacity, targeting leukemia stem cells while sparing normal HSCs. Mechanistically, we identify a novel Ran-GTP-dependent role for CSE1L in regulating pre-60S ribosomal subunit export in AML. Collectively, these data identify nucleocytoplasmic transport and ribosomal subunit export as enriched dependencies in pediatric/AYA AML and establish CSE1L-mediated export as a leukemic vulnerability.

papers.title: Mutant ASXL1 exacerbates CALR-mutant myeloproliferative neoplasms by enhancing a distinct megakaryocyte differentiation program.
papers.abstract: ASXL1 mutations confer a poor prognosis in myeloid neoplasms, including in CALR-mutated myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN). We generated Calr-Asxl1 co-mutant mice and found more severe thrombocytosis and increased splenomegaly, compared with Calr single-mutant animals. Calr-Asxl1 co-mutant megakaryocytes displayed more pronounced morphological abnormalities and enhanced emperipolesis characteristic of inflammation. Concordant with this, a differentiation trajectory directly to megakaryocytes from hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) was more prominent in Calr-Asxl1 co-mutant mice. In this non-canonical trajectory, where megakaryocyte-biased HSCs directly differentiate into megakaryocyte progenitors, we found upregulation of Mef2c, a key transcriptional regulator of megakaryocyte lineage commitment. Mature Calr-Asxl1 co-mutant megakaryocytes displayed an enhanced proinflammatory transcriptional state, whereas the transcriptional signature of Calr-Asxl1 co-mutant HSCs was indicative of inflammation-resistance. Genotyping of transcriptomes (GoT) confirmed an activated megakaryocytic differentiation program in CALR-ASXL1 co-mutant HSCs in primary human MPN bone marrow. These findings link the enhanced severity of CALR-ASXL1 co-mutant MPN to altered megakaryocyte differentiation and help explain some of the biological basis for the more severe MPN phenotype observed in patients.

papers.title: The amygdaloid complex: from morphology to neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: The amygdaloid complex is one of the most structurally and functionally heterogeneous regions of the mammalian brain, acting as an integrative node between sensory, mnemonic and visceral systems. It comprises a set of subnuclei whose cytoarchitectural differentiation, neurochemical profiles and anatomical boundaries have been debated since the earliest descriptions. This heterogeneity is established during ontogenetic development, assembling progenitors from pallial and subpallial domains, and preoptic and hypothalamic territories, resulting in a highly connected network. Maturation is not complete at birth, the amygdala changes through childhood and adolescence, leaving a protracted window of environmental sensitivity. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have added a molecular layer to this framework, resolving populations that no single marker separates, and set explicit limits on the resolution at which rodent-derived subdivisions can be transferred to the human amygdala. Together these levels of description provide a structural framework for understanding its functions, which include emotional regulation and conditioned fear, social and sexual behaviours, decision-making, reward and punishment processing, empathy and memory modulation. Cross-species comparison reveals further variation, particularly the expansion of the basolateral complex in primates and the redistribution of neurons towards the lateral nucleus in humans. In summary, the amygdala acts as a densely connected hub with a broad role not only in physiological and psychological health but also in disease states; indeed, the amygdala is affected early in several neurodegenerative disorders, and in some (notably limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy and argyrophilic grain disease) it is among the first regions in which pathology is detected.

papers.title: Isoimperatorin regulates hepatic fibrosis through LXRα/β-HMGB1/NLRP3 axis: insights into the apoptosis of activated hepatic stellate cells in hepatic microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Hepatic fibrosis is a pathological response to persistent liver injury, characterized by activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. Isoimperatorin (ISOIM), a coumarin derivative isolated from Angelica dahurica, has been reported to possess analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties. This study investigated the hepatoprotective potential of ISOIM and its underlying mechanisms against hepatic fibrosis. C57BL/6J mice were intraperitoneally injected with thioacetamide (TAA, 100-200 mg·kg) for 5 weeks and received ISOIM (5 or 8 mg·kg) administration. HSCs and LX-2 were stimulated with transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β, 10 nmol·L) or conditioned medium from lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-primed THP-1 (LPS-MØ-CM), followed by ISOIM (0.78, 1.56, 3.125 μmol·L) treatment. In TAA-induced mice, ISOIM reduced serum transaminases, attenuated ECM deposition and histopathological damage, alleviated inflammatory responses, and decreased hepatocyte apoptosis. In activated HSCs, ISOIM inhibited ECM accumulation, reduced inflammatory cytokine expression and promoted apoptotic signaling. Mechanistically, ISOIM showed a potential interaction with LXRα/β, reduced HMGB1-associated inflammatory signaling, and suppressed activation of the HMGB1/NLRP3 signaling, accompanied by enhanced caspase-3-mediated apoptotic signaling in activated HSCs. These effects were consistent with those of the LXRα/β agonist GW3965 and were markedly attenuated by LXRβ or LXRα silencing. In addition, ISOIM regulated LXRα/β and the HMGB1-NLRP3 axis, reduced α-SMA expression, and promoted apoptotic signaling in LX-2 cultured with LPS-MØ-CM. Collectively, ISOIM exerted hepatoprotective effects by activating LXRα/β, inhibiting HMGB1/NLRP3 signaling, and promoting apoptosis of activated HSCs within the hepatic microenvironment.

title.#text: EPCR expression marks CD150deeply dormant long-term hematopoietic stem cells.

papers.abstract: Cell surface expression of the Slam family member CD150 is widely used for the prospective isolation of multipotent long-term hematopoietic stem cells (LT-HSCs). Here, we identify a bona fide endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR)CD150HSC subset, termed LT-HSC2, that sustains serial multi-lineage reconstitution. Long-term label-retaining assays reveal that LT-HSC2s are more deeply dormant than conventional EPCRCD150LT-HSC1s, exhibit reduced cell cycle activation in response to inflammatory stress, and preserve stemness for prolonged periods in vivo. Moreover, combining EPCR with established HSC and multipotent progenitor (MPP) markers resolves the earliest stages of lineage divergence toward megakaryocytic/erythroid-biased CD150and lymphoid-biased CD150trajectories. Thus, EPCR expression in HSCs and MPPs is associated with increased stemness, whereas CD150 expression does not encompass the full spectrum of long-term repopulating HSCs. Our findings establish EPCRCD150LT-HSC2s as a distinct, exceptionally dormant stem-cell subset and reveal an additional layer of HSC heterogeneity governing self-renewal, decreased stress sensitvity. and earliest lineage priming.

papers.title: Exploring the Mechanism of DEHP Promoting Hepatic Fibrosis Based on Network Toxicology by Triggering Lipophagy-Dependent Hepatic Stellate Cell Activation.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
papers.abstract: Di(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (DEHP), a common environmental endocrine disruptor and agricultural organic pollutant, has drawn wide concern for its hepatotoxicity. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying DEHP-induced hepatic fibrosis remain unclear. Through network toxicology analysis, lipid metabolism and autophagy pathways are involved in DEHP-related hepatic fibrosis. Subchronic DEHP exposure (50-500 mg/kg) induced dose-dependent hepatic fibrosis in mice, while its metabolite MEHP synergized with TGF-β1 to promote LX2 cell activation in vitro. Crucially, MEHP activates lipophagy by targeting Beclin1, thereby mobilizing energy for the activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). Attenuating autophagy with 3-Methyladenine (3-MA) or Chloroquine (CQ), or via Beclin1 knockdown, all rescued the activation phenotype induced by MEHP. These results suggest that DEHP acts as a trigger for fibrosis, promoting this process by inducing the activation of HSCs. This work identifies the lipophagy pathway as a crucial mechanistic link between environmental toxin exposure and HSC-mediated hepatic fibrosis progression.

papers.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential and Bone Mineral Density in Cohorts from Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine.
papers.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
papers.abstract: A somatic mutation causing clonal expansion in hematopoietic stem cells (HSC), but not resulting in hematologic malignancy, is termed clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP). CHIP is associated with non-hematologic disorders, including accelerated atherosclerosis, heart failure, ischemic stroke, gout, liver disease, and kidney disease. Because osteoclasts are derived from the macrophage-monocyte lineage of HSCs, changes in the bone marrow niche due to CHIP may drive changes in BMD. To investigate whether CHIP may be related to BMD, we used CHIP mutation calls from the Trans-omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) whole genome sequencing data and DXA derived BMD from multiple cohorts. Data from the the Amish cohort, Cardiovascular Health Study, the Framingham Heart Study, San Antonio Family Study, and the Women's Health Initiative were combined for analysis. Multiple linear regression was used to determine the association between CHIP mutation status and BMD, adjusting for cohort, age, age,2 sex, and, for family-based cohorts, empiric kinship estimated from genotype data. CHIP mutation status was analyzed both as a binary variable (any CHIP mutation) and as an ordinal variable (no CHIP mutation, 1 CHIP mutation in any gene, two or more CHIP mutations in a single gene, two or more CHIP mutations in different genes). A total of 3368 samples had both CHIP and BMD data, and 10.9% of samples contained any CHIP mutation. The presence of any CHIP mutations was not associated with either femoral neck or lumbar spine BMD; however, the presence of two or more CHIP mutations in different genes was positively associated with LSBMD (beta = 0.36, p = .015). We found no overall association between the presence of CHIP mutations and BMD in a large, diverse sample of genomes. Our findings of greater BMD in persons harboring multiple CHIP mutations confirm mouse models demonstrating that Dnmt3a and Tet2 mutations independently cause increased B

papers.title: Hesperetin-loaded transethosomes for management of skin cancer: formulation and optimization by Box-Behnken design and in vitro, ex vivo, and dermatokinetic studies.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop and optimize hesperetin-loaded transethosomes (HSP-TEs) to ameliorate skin cancer, yet enhancing skin permeability, deposition, and stability. HSP-TEs were prepared using thin-film hydration and optimized through a Box-Behnken design (BBD). The optimized formulation exhibited a vesicle size of 134.27 ± 3.17 nm, polydispersity index of 0.209 ± 0.006, zeta potential of - 27.39 ± 0.53 mV, and entrapment efficiency of 90.33 ± 3.88%, confirming nanoscale stability and uniformity. HSP-TEs were further incorporated into a Carbopol-based HSP-TE loaded gel (HSP-TEG) for topical application. Comparative in vitro release studies revealed sustained release from HSP-TEs (71.77 ± 6.79%), followed by HSP-TEG (60.03 ± 4.13%) at 24 h, whereas significantly lower release was observed from hesperetin suspension (HSP-S, 32.23 ± 5.09%) and hesperetin-suspension gel (HSP-SG, 25.76 ± 3.55%) at 24 h. Ex vivo permeation studies demonstrated superior skin penetration from HSP-TEs (63.70 ± 5.19%) and HSP-TEG (51.03 ± 3.12%) compared to HSP-S (27.23 ± 2.16%) and HSP-SG (23.87 ± 1.09%) at 24 h. Confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) analysis of HSP-TEs revealed greater skin permeability. Dermatokinetic analysis confirmed enhanced epidermal and dermal drug deposition from HSP-TEG. The cytotoxicity studies in A431 epidermoid carcinoma cells demonstrated greater time- and concentration-dependent anticancer effects for HSP-TEs relative to free drug (p < 0.05). The optimized formulation revealed sustained release and improved permeability and stability, suggesting a promising platform for management skin cancer.

papers.title: Method-Dependent Variation in Stomatal Trait Estimation and Its Functional Implications in Oryza Species.
papers.abstract: Reliable quantification of stomatal traits is essential for understanding plant gas exchange and its responses to environmental changes. However, grasses present methodological challenges due to their complex leaf surface topography and the distinctive dumbbell-shaped stomata arranged in longitudinal rows. Here, we combined a literature-based synthesis with comparative experiments to assess how measurement methods influence stomatal trait estimates and to characterize interspecific variation and environmental plasticity across Oryza species. Literature-based synthesis revealed large cross-study variations in reported stomatal density, with apparent differences of up to one order of magnitude among studies using SEM and impression-based methods, although this variation may also reflect differences in genotypes, environments, developmental stages, and sampling protocols. Experimental comparisons confirmed consistent differences between SEM and imprint measurements, although the differences were smaller in magnitude. Across species, stomatal density, guard-cell length, and guard-cell width exhibited substantial diversity and conserved rankings across environments, while guard-cell length showed greater environmental sensitivity. Moreover, method-dependent differences significantly affected estimates of anatomical maximum stomatal conductance. Our results demonstrate that measurement methodology is an important source of uncertainty in stomatal trait estimation, even within the same leaf, and that Oryza species display broad interspecific morphological variations but comparatively constrained environmental responses. These findings highlight the need to standardize imaging protocols and to account for method-dependent differences for accurate interpretation of relationships between stomatal morphology and functions in rice.

papers.title: The maternal-fetal interface is an early hematopoietic niche enriched in distinct erythro-myeloid progenitors.
papers.abstract: Embryonic hematopoiesis is thought to occur exclusively in the extraembryonic yolk sac before hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise in the aorta-gonad-mesonephros region. Here we identify a previously unrecognized hematopoietic site at the maternal-fetal interface in mice, termed MIXER (Maternally Interfaced eXtraEmbRyonic) tissue, which develops contemporaneously with the yolk sac and exhibits robust hematopoietic activity. MIXER contains abundant hematopoietic precursors, including classical CSF1Rerythro-myeloid progenitors and a unique embryonic CD4CSF1RErythro-Myeloid PRogenitOR (eEMPROR) population. Lineage-tracing experiments demonstrate that eEMPROR cells contribute to select macrophage subpopulations during fetal development, primarily in the perivascular space. Notably, early human placental villi, before HSC emergence, also harbor CD4nucleated erythrocytes, indicating a conserved hematopoietic role for the maternal-fetal interface. These findings establish MIXER as an anatomically distinct niche for embryonic hematopoiesis and expand the developmental map of blood cell emergence in mammals.

papers.title: Epigallocatechin gallate and thermal cycling‑stimulation synergistically promote apoptosis in A549 cells via endoplasmic reticulum stress‑induced calcium ion dysregulation and oxidative stress.
papers.abstract: Non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as the predominant subtype of lung cancer, presents a considerable clinical challenge due to its high rates of recurrence and the significant adverse effects associated with conventional therapeutic modalities. In response to these challenges, the present study has explored the combined anticancer effects of epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) together with thermal cycling‑stimulation (TCS). The findings obtained demonstrated that the combination of EGCG and TCS led to a synergistic decrease in the viability of A549 and NCI‑H460 NSCLC cells, whereas IMR‑90 normal lung fibroblasts exhibited minimal cytotoxic effects. Further investigations revealed that EGCG could mitigate the TCS‑induced upregulation of the heat shock proteins (HSPs) HSP70 and HSP105, whereas the expression levels of proteasome subunits were concurrently decreased. These alterations were accompanied by the disruption of proteostasis, and also by the activation of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress‑associated pathways. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition studies suggested a mutual interplay between inositol 1,4,5‑trisphosphate receptor‑mediated ER Ca2+ release and an excessive production of reactive oxygen species, ultimately causing the cells to undergo mitochondrial apoptosis. In summary, the present study has shown that the combined treatment of EGCG and TCS reduces the required dosage of EGCG, while also attenuating TCS‑induced heat shock responses. Consequently, the present study offers a novel and promisingproof‑of‑concept strategy for treating NSCLC.

papers.title: Redox-metabolic cascade NIR-II prodrug for synchronizing compensatory HSPs/P-gp feedback with mitophagy flux impairment against intrinsic thermotolerance.
papers.abstract: The intrinsic proteostasis of HSPs/P-gp remains formidable barriers in the multidrug resistance (MDR) and thermotolerance. To dismantle the compensatory HSPs and P-gp defense axis, we developed a metabolic reprogramming NIR-II nanoprodrug Lipid 2-DG@Au/DOX-ss, using gold liposome-nanorod loaded disulfide-doxorubicin prodrug DOX-ss and 2-deoxy-d-glucose (2-DG). Results revealed 2-DG dose-dependent metabolic perturbations of ATP, glucose, NAD, LDH. Coupled with a 24.01-fold ROS enhancement, a 5.05-fold PINK1 surge, a 0.65-fold LC3-II accumulation, 0.29-fold p62 increase, S-phase arrest (up to 64%), intensive mitophagy flux impairment was initiated to terminal cell death via NF-κB/PINK1/LC3-II pathway. Proteomic analysis further elucidates the concurrent inhibition of HSP70 (A12A)/90/B1(27)-mediated protein folding with P-gp efflux pump downregulation and the disruption of mitochondrial autophagic clearance, as well as unveiling the potent in immune modulation, ferroptosis, and calcium homeostasis. This bioenergetics-derived nanoprodrug with HSPs/P-gp compensation and mitophagy impairment provides a precise approach for eradicating recalcitrant MDR malignancies.

papers.title: Acaudiolide attenuates MASH-related liver fibrosis through covalent engagement of SMAD4 and blockade of p-SMAD2/3 nuclear translocation.
papers.abstract: Hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation is a central driver of fibrosis progression in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), yet effective antifibrotic pharmacotherapies remain limited. Here, we identify acaudiolide, a sulfur-bridged symmetric dimeric macrodiolide isolated from the fungus Acaulium sp. H-JQSF, as a natural-product lead that suppresses HSC activation and experimental liver fibrosis. In a Western diet (WD)/CClmurine model of MASH, acaudiolide reduced collagen deposition, alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) expression and fibrogenic gene expression. Transcriptomic profiling of HSCs showed that acaudiolide antagonized transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-driven profibrotic programs. Mechanistically, acaudiolide did not measurably alter SMAD2/3 phosphorylation but markedly reduced the nuclear accumulation of phosphorylated SMAD2/3 (p-SMAD2/3). Integration of Connectivity Map (CMap) analysis with isotopic tandem orthogonal proteolysis-activity-based protein profiling (isoTOP-ABPP) chemical proteomics nominated SMAD4 as a candidate covalent target of acaudiolide. Covalent docking suggested Cys363 as a potential engagement site, and co-immunoprecipitation showed that acaudiolide weakened the association of SMAD4 with p-SMAD2/3. These findings support a model in which acaudiolide interferes with SMAD complex assembly, thereby attenuating TGF-β-dependent profibrotic transcription and HSC activation. Collectively, our data nominate acaudiolide as a preclinical antifibrotic lead and SMAD4 as a potentially tractable downstream node for pharmacological modulation of TGF-β signaling in MASH-related fibrosis.

papers.title: Interactive effect of childhood adversity and HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation on alexithymia in adolescents.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood adversity increases risk for affective symptoms, including alexithymia, a transdiagnostic emotion-processing difficulty common in adolescence. Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis-related genetic variation may contribute to individual differences in sensitivity to adverse environments. This study examined whether an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) moderated the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia. METHODS: The present study addressed this issue in a sample of 460 adolescents (Mage = 12.73, SD = 0.72; 54.1% female) who completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale. Saliva samples were collected for deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) genotyping, and an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) was constructed from six candidate polymorphisms. Hierarchical regression and re-parameterized regression analyses were conducted. RESULTS: Childhood adversity was positively associated with alexithymia. HPA-axis MGPS moderated this association. Specifically, adolescents with high HPA-axis MGPS exhibited higher levels of alexithymia when exposed to high childhood adversity but lower levels when exposed to low childhood adversity, providing preliminary support for the differential susceptibility model. LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the findings require replication in longitudinal, clinically enriched, and more diverse samples. CONCLUSIONS: HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation may function as a biological sensitivity factor in the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia. These findings extend gene-environment interaction research to alexithymia and highlight individual differences in adolescents' emotional responses to adversity.

papers.title: Environmental sensitivity and perceived social support in relation to adolescent eating disorder symptoms.
papers.abstract: Eating disorders (EDs) frequently emerge during adolescence and are influenced by both individual and contextual factors. Among these, perceived social support has generally been associated with better outcomes, although findings remain inconsistent and may depend on both the source of support and individual differences in responsiveness to environmental inputs. The present study examined the role of Environmental Sensitivity (ES) and perceived social support in adolescent ED symptoms, focusing on different sources of support and their potential interaction within a vantage sensitivity framework. A sample of 466 adolescents (51.61% female; M = 14.80) completed self-report measures of ED symptoms, ES, and perceived social support. At a bivariate level, higher perceived support from family, teachers, friends, and peers was associated with lower ED symptoms. In covariate-adjusted models, only teachers' and family's support remained a significant predictor, while peer-related sources were no longer associated with ED symptoms. ES was consistently and positively associated with ED symptoms. Contrary to hypotheses, ES did not moderate the association between overall perceived social support and ED symptoms. Exploratory analyses suggested a sex-specific pattern, whereby the association between perceived social support and ED symptoms appeared to vary as a function of ES among males, but not females. These findings suggest that the association between social support and adolescent ED symptoms may depend on its source. Moreover, ES was consistently associated with ED symptoms. Exploratory analyses revealed that evidence for differential responsiveness to supportive contexts may vary by ES among males.

papers.title: Five-in-One NIR-II phototheranostic nanomedicine for glioblastoma multiforme: Unlocking bio-barriers and photothermal-ferroptotic amplification.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) remains a formidable therapeutic challenge due to its aggressive behavior, complex biological barriers, and high recurrence rates. Near-infrared II (NIR-II) phototheranostic nanomedicine has emerged as a promising strategy, offering deeper tissue penetration and enhanced photothermal effects for GBM treatment. Herein, we demonstrate an effective molecular design strategy that leverages expanded free space within aggregates to boost non-radiative decay and improve photothermal conversion efficiency (PCE). Based on this approach, we create a nanomedicine using holo-transferrin (holo-Tf) to encapsulate optimized phototheranostic agents (NDA-18). This nanosystem achieves efficient blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration via transferrin receptor (TfR)-mediated transcytosis and selective tumor accumulation. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, the nanomedicine enables precise photothermal therapy (PTT) while concurrently triggering ferroptosis. This ferroptosis process further enhances the PTT efficacy by suppressing heat shock proteins (HSPs), resulting in an enhanced synergistic antitumor effect. Remarkably, this one-step self-assembled nanomedicine integrates five critical functions: from BBB penetration and tumor targeting to dual-mode imaging and synergistic PTT-ferroptosis therapy. In conclusion, we have successfully developed an innovative nanoplatform that unites rational molecular design, bioengineering, and synergistic therapy for GBM treatment.

papers.title: Elevated asymmetric dimethylarginine drives hematopoietic stem cell metabolic reprogramming and dysfunction in chronic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is commonly linked to hematopoietic abnormalities beyond the well-recognized anemia, with underlying mechanisms poorly understood. Here, we show that asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA), which accumulates in the CKD microenvironment, perturbs hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) homeostasis. Clinical data analysis reveals that serum ADMA levels rise with CKD progression and inversely correlate with the myeloid-to-lymphoid ratio. Notably, ADMA compromises HSC quiescence and long-term repopulating capacity, as observed in CKD mouse models established by 5/6 nephrectomy. Further investigations demonstrate that ADMA hyperactivates mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling, promoting the transition from glycolysis to oxidative phosphorylation and inducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) overproduction in HSCs. Mechanistically, ADMA binds with high affinity to protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit Bβ (PPP2R2B), relieving its inhibition of mTOR signaling. Inhibition of mTOR signaling by rapamycin or clearance of ROS by N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) reverses ADMA-induced HSC functional defects. Collectively, our findings identify ADMA as a key mediator of CKD-associated hematopoietic dysfunction via the PPP2R2B-mTOR-mitochondria axis, providing a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Adult hematopoietic stem cells activate a normally fetal-restricted program to functionally expand ex vivo.
papers.abstract: The ability to robustly expand transplantable hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) ex vivo enables basic science and clinical therapies otherwise hindered by the scarcity of these self-renewing multipotent cells. Despite recent improvements in long-term ex vivo HSC expansion conditions, the molecular mechanisms required for successful ex vivo expansion of functional HSCs remain unknown. Here we characterized the ex vivo expansion potential of HSCs from mouse fetal liver, young bone marrow, and aged bone marrow at the functional and molecular levels. We find that Lin28b, the in vivo fetal-restricted gene, contributes to the mechanism of both fetal and adult ex vivo HSC expansion. The expression of Lin28b correlates with reconstitution potential, with higher levels observed in HSCs expanded from the fetal liver and young adults. By contrast, expanded aged HSCs fail to robustly express Lin28b and also fail to stably reconstitute the hematopoietic system following transplantation. Consistent with a functional role for this fetal program in ex vivo expanded HSCs, Lin28b-deficient HSCs display aging-associated molecular and functional features following ex vivo expansion cultures. Importantly, Lin28b overexpression during ex vivo expansion was sufficient to enhance reconstitution potential of aged HSCs. In summary, we identify Lin28b as an important regulator of functional HSC expansion ex vivo, suggesting novel opportunities for HSC rejuvenation and clinical applications.

papers.title: Demethylzeylasteral Targets the Sp1/AGAP2 Axis to Impair Autophagic Flux and Induce Apoptosis in Hepatic Stellate Cells.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Chronic liver injury-induced liver fibrosis, if left untreated, can progress to cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma, posing a serious threat to human health. Our previous study demonstrated that the natural product demethylzeylasteral (T-96) alleviates liver fibrosis by suppressing ArfGAP with GTPase domain, ankyrin repeat and PH domain 2 (AGAP2) expression. However, the molecular mechanism underlying T-96-mediated regulation of AGAP2 remains unclear. This study aimed to clarify this mechanism and explore T-96's role in liver fibrogenesis. METHODS: A series of molecular biological experiments (e.g., promoter activity assay, co-immunoprecipitation, Western blot, and immunofluorescence) were performed to identify the transcription factor regulating AGAP2. The interaction between T-96 and the transcription factor, as well as the degradation pathway of the latter, were investigated. Additionally, in vitro experiments were conducted to evaluate the effects of T-96 on autophagy, apoptosis, and activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). RESULTS: We identified Sp1 as the transcription factor mediating AGAP2 promoter activity. Mechanistically, T-96 directly bound to Sp1 and promoted its degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, thereby downregulating AGAP2 expression. Furthermore, T-96 impairs autophagic flux and induces apoptosis in activated HSCs through specific targeting of Sp1. CONCLUSIONS: This study delineates a novel regulatory axis centered on Sp1 (T-96/Sp1/AGAP2) in liver fibrosis, wherein T-96 binds to Sp1 to promote its ubiquitination and degradation, subsequently inhibiting AGAP2 expression and inducing autophagic flux impairment/apoptosis in activated HSCs to alleviate liver fibrosis. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for developing targeted therapeutics and clinical strategies for fibrotic liver disease.

papers.title: Parental support moderates the interaction of COMT and BDNF genotypes with early life adversity on problem gambling severity index scores among young adults.
papers.abstract: The development of gambling-related harm and gambling disorder involves several genetic and environmental factors. However, how these factors interact to influence the development and whether such interactions confer to diathesis-stress or differential susceptibility models remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, data from the Survey of Adolescent Life in Västmanland (SALVe cohort) were utilized, Participants provided a saliva sample for genotyping, completed early life adversity (ELA) and Parents as Social Construct (PASCQ) surveys at age 17, and the Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) at age 23. A total of 391 participants (54% females) with complete data were included for analysis. Negative binomial models were utilized to examine the interaction between candidate genes (COMT, BDNF, and DRD2), ELA, and parental support in PGSI scores. Interactions between COMT and BDNF, ELA, and parental support were found but not for DRD2, (β = -0.01 and -0.009, 95% CI [-0.02, -0.006 and -0.01, -0.005], p = 2.2 × 10and 1.2 × 10respectively). The interactions remained significant after accounting for sex interactions, p = 0.005. Notably, evidence for a differential susceptibility framework was found in gambling-related harm scores. Participants with the major allele for both COMT and BDNF displayed plasticity by exhibiting higher PGSI scores when exposed to weak parental support but lower PGSI scores in strong parental support despite higher ELA scores. Positive parental support acted as a protective factor against the genetic sensitivity of gambling-related harm. Studies pursuing the interplay between genetic and environmental factors would benefit from including positive environments that may mitigate the risk associated with adverse environments.

papers.title: Identification of the HSP gene family in wild Daurian ground squirrel (Spermophilus dauricus) and analysis of their expression during different hibernation stages.
papers.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part A, Molecular & integrative physiology
papers.abstract: Hibernation is an extreme form of seasonal heterothermy that enables animals to survive under harsh environmental conditions and provides valuable natural models for investigating the physiological mechanisms underlying stress tolerance. The Daurian ground squirrel (Spermophilus dauricus) is a small burrowing mammal that exhibits pronounced seasonal changes in activity and naturally undergoes hibernation, making it a useful model for elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying hibernation. Heat shock proteins (HSPs) are highly conserved molecular chaperones involved in protein homeostasis and cellular stress responses. A total of 40 HSP genes were identified in the Daurian ground squirrel and grouped into six subfamilies, consisting of three small HSPs (sHSPs), 26 HSP40s, six HSP70s, three HSP90s, one HSP60, and one HSP110. Comprehensive analyses of molecular characteristics, conserved domains, gene structures, phylogenetic relationships, and chromosomal distributions revealed substantial evolutionary diversity within the HSP40 family. Although members of the DNAJA, DNAJB, and DNAJC subfamilies shared several conserved structural features, differences were also observed in their molecular characteristics and evolutionary relationships. To investigate their expression dynamics during hibernation, the transcript levels of HSP40 genes in the liver tissues of the Daurian ground squirrels at different hibernation stages were quantified using the real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Most of the HSP40 genes examined exhibited broadly similar expression trends throughout the hibernation cycle, although individual genes showed different temporal expression profiles. These findings suggest that HSP40 genes undergo differential transcriptional regulation during hibernation and may be involved in the physiological responses associated with hepatic adaptation to the hibernation state. papers.title: Biliverdin reductase A deficiency reveals sex- and brain region-specific vulnerability to high-fat diet feeding.
papers.abstract: How the brain senses and responds to early metabolic stress, and why this process fails differently across sexes and regions, remains poorly understood. Here we show that biliverdin reductase A (BVRA) loss is associated with sex- and brain region-specific effects in response to high-fat diet (HFD) feeding, impairing insulin signaling and mitochondrial responses in selected brain regions while being associated with adaptive liver remodeling and improved systemic glucose handling in female mice. Using wild-type and whole-body BVRA-deficient mice of both sexes exposed to short-term high-fat diet (HFD) followed by dietary normalization, we show that BVRA loss is sufficient to induce cortical insulin resistance within just one week, phenocopying eight weeks of HFD and preceding detectable oxidative distress or mitochondrial failure. This sequence supports a model in which dysfunctional insulin signaling may represent an early event in the cascade of brain metabolic injury. The frontal cortex is the earliest and most vulnerable brain region, whereas the hippocampus shows delayed and milder alterations, suggesting brain region-specific vulnerability to HFD. Strikingly, F mice develop cognitive impairments indistinguishable from M mice despite substantially milder molecular alterations, revealing a sex-specific dissociation between molecular severity and functional outcome. After dietary normalization, M mice show partial recovery of cortical insulin signaling, mitochondrial function, and recognition memory. In contrast, F mice exhibit progressive BVRA decline, worsening insulin signaling uncoupling, and persistent cognitive deficits that outlast dietary exposure - revealing a metabolic memory encoded at the molecular level. These findings identify BVRA loss as a potential causal and sex-biased determinant of brain metabolic vulnerability, with implications for understanding the sex-differential susceptibility to insulin resistance-related neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Biochemical responses in Magallana bilineata: Leveraging oxidative stress for management of tropical estuaries.
papers.abstract: Oysters, known for their environmental sensitivity, are potential bioindicators of stress in aquatic ecosystems. This study investigates the influence of environmental stressors, including salinity, temperature, and dissolved oxygen, on the enzymatic activities of Glutathione S-transferase (GST) and Catalase (CAT) in the gills and digestive glands of the slipper oyster, Magallana bilineata. Monthly sampling was conducted at Setiu Wetland, Terengganu (Malaysia), during the monsoon. Significant monthly variations were observed in temperature (p < 0.0001) and salinity (p < 0.05), but not for dissolved oxygen. Protein concentrations, CAT, and GST activity in gills and digestive glands showed significant differences (p < 0.05) between months, indicating the effect of environmental changes on the physiology of M. bilineata. Spearman's rank correlation revealed a strong positive correlation between protein concentration and GST activity in gills (ρ = 0.68), and a moderate positive correlation between CAT activity in the digestive gland and salinity (ρ = 0.56). Principal component analysis (PCA) explained 47.6% of the total variance, with the first two components (PC1 and PC2) accounting for 27.8% and 19.8%, respectively. These findings suggest that CAT and GST activities in M. bilineata vary with seasonal environmental conditions and may serve as potential biomarker endpoints for future biomonitoring studies. However, additional validation using reference sites and controlled exposure experiments is required to distinguish natural physiological variation from stress-specific responses.

title.#text: Age-related IGF-1 decline permits a redox-sensitive transcriptional shift that directs hematopoiesis toward a CCR2myeloid fate.

papers.abstract: Aging reshapes hematopoiesis toward myelopoiesis, particularly increased output of classical monocytes, contributing to immunosenescence. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify that aging drives hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) to progressively commit to a CCR2monocyte fate along a defined lineage trajectory, which is executed through a redox-sensitive transcriptional cascade. We find that the age-related decline in bone marrow IGF-1 is the upstream niche signal that releases suppression of the oxidative stress/NF-κB/IRF8 axis, allowing this cascade to redirect early progenitors toward a CCR2myeloid-primed fate. Functional assays confirm that cells following this CCR2trajectory drive myeloid-biased hematopoiesis and directly contribute to age-associated immunosuppression. Our work delineates a hierarchical pathway from niche decay to lineage redirection, establishing the CCR2fate trajectory as a key driver of immunosenescence and a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Enhancing the Functionality of Human Bone Marrow-Derived Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Using Signaling Modulators.
papers.abstract: Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (BM-MSCs) possess an inherent capacity to support hematopoiesis in vitro. As a result, they are often used as feeder layers for the ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) or coinfused with HSCs to improve the success of clinical transplants. However, MSCs isolated from non-hematopoietic tissues such as adipose or dental tissue may not be as effective as BM-MSCs in supporting hematopoiesis. Additionally, BM-MSCs tend to lose their functional ability after extended in vitro culture, which is necessary for producing sufficient cell numbers for clinical use. These limitations underscore the importance of pretreating MSCs with suitable signaling modulators to boost their functionality. Reliable in vitro assays play a crucial role in finding such signaling compounds and evaluating their effects on MSCs. Conventional assays, such as long-term-culture-initiating assay (LTC-IC assay) or colony-forming-unit assay (CFU assay), chemotactic migration assays (e.g., Transwell assay), etc., primarily evaluate the functional competence of HSCs and HSPCs, but provide little insight into the hematopoiesis-supportive capacity of MSCs. This chapter describes two such assays: one is designed to assess the hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell (HSPC)-supporting capacity of primed MSCs, and the other is specifically aimed at their ability to support the growth of primitive HSCs. These assays can serve as initial screens to test the impact, whether positive or negative, synergistic or antagonistic, of known signaling compounds, bioactive peptides, growth factors, and cytokines on MSC function or to discover new entities that could boost the functionality of MSCs.

papers.title: Using patient iPSC-derived retinal pigment epithelium to evaluate differential susceptibility to MEK inhibitor-associated retinopathy.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Compare the effect of MEK inhibition on iPSC-derived retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) cells generated from a patient who developed MEK inhibitor-Associated Retinopathy (MEKAR) versus a patient who did not develop retinopathy. This is an exploratory, hypothesis-generating comparison of one donor line per clinical phenotype. DESIGN: Exploratory case-control comparison (one patient-derived line per phenotype) SUBJECTS: Two female patients with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 who were treated with MEK inhibitors. One patient developed MEKAR, the other did not. METHODS: RPE were generated from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) from these two patients. These hiPSC-derived RPE were treated with selumetinib for 10 days. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Phagocytic activity and changes in gene expression. RESULTS: As previously reported, there was a significant increase in internalized rhodopsin in phagocytosis assays, yet this was only found in hiPSC-derived RPE from the patient who developed MEKAR. Selumetinib decreased expression of genes related to fluid transport and cell volume, including aquaporins and solute transporters. At baseline, cells from the patients without MEKAR had higher expression of these genes. Interestingly, selumetinib-induced changes in gene expression only reached statistical significance in cells from the patient who did not develop MEKAR, suggesting these changes may be a compensatory protective mechanism. Patients susceptible to forming MEKAR may have increased phagocytosis without a compensatory change in expression of genes related to fluid flux, thereby inhibiting their ability to transport fluid out of the subretinal space. papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals atorvastatin modulates the tumor microenvironment to suppress breast cancer liver metastatic outgrowth.
papers.abstract: Metastatic breast cancer remains incurable, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic strategies. Epidemiological and preclinical evidence suggests statins suppress metastatic outgrowth, however the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We employed high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (ST) to explore the cellular composition and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the metastatic microenvironment following atorvastatin treatment. papers.title: HIF-1α-ASS1 axis drives reprogramming of arginine metabolism controls hepatic stellate cell activation in hepatic fibrosis.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.abstract: Dysregulated arginine metabolism promotes hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and liver fibrosis. However, the mechanisms underlying arginine hosmeostasis in hepatic fibrogenesis and therapeutic targeting remain unclear. Using Multicellular hepatic spheroid (MCHS) models recapitulating in vivo liver fibrosis, we investigated the effects of arginine deprivation or supplementation. Holotomography and quantitative imaging approaches characterized cellular and molecular fibrogenic changes.
